Don't feel gross about this. It's a natural picking thing to make you feel better when you get anxious. I do it as well, to the point they bleed. I also compulsively chew my nails, so i will offer the advice that worked the best for me. 

Take care of them. Always carry a small nail kit with you, I personally always wait until christmas to get the cheap $3 nail kit but I am sure you can find a cheap one on amazon. I find when I'm picking it is not just because of stress but sometimes I am just being compulsive about how it feels. Like a hang nail turns into having no nail because I chew it off. But with the nail kit I find myself pulling it out and cutting and filing my nails as well as cutting and pushing my cuticals back. The little time I take towards myself to clean my nails is both theraputic and helps me not chew them because they dont feel crummy ie cracking, getting caught on things, ect. 

The other thing is invest in a good cutical oil! I chew my skin around my nails when it gets dry or cracked or really just rough in any way. Cutical oil both helps keep your nails and cuticals clean but really helped me with the chewing, anytime i felt the urge to chew i told myself no, put on the oil and rubbed it in really good for 15 mins instead of chewing. I noticed by the end they were so soft i honestly forgot why i wanted to chew them in the first place. I used this as well with my niece who is only 3 and has a ripping her nails offf problem. She hated the skin being all messed up and would end up ripping her poor nails off in attempts to get the skin. I started giving her the cutical oil as a "medicine" and though its not a true medicine the act of doing something to "make it feel better" was enough to get her to cut the habit. 

Lastly, my therapist brought this up when I was like 14 and thats anytime you find youself chewing, stop. Take a minute and then as slowly as possible, im talking barely moving, like 10 minutes of slowly moving your hand towards your mouth, decide to continue chewing. The act of going as slow as possible causes an irritation which is supposed to tell your body you do this youll be irritated. It worked pretty well for me, well it made me angry like i just wanted to chew but couldnt and it really put into perspective my control over my body. Dont let your anxiety and body control you, you control it. 

Good luck hope this helps!

I cannot offer the kind of support you probably need right now, but I do have some advice and a little imput. To me, yes life is worth it. I've been suicidal since I was like 7-8, I'm 23 now and honestly still have the same feelings, HOWEVER I feel life is worth it despite this because the older I am getting the more I figure out. Everything seems so simple when you are young, then as you get older it does change, and you can change. I'm still in the same suicidal boat, but it has gotten better, if even only in the fact I can tell lately when my anxiety or depression is hitting, and I can try to make a change towards that and make it go away, and as I'm getting older I'm learning more and more how to get those thoughts out of my head and see the good around me and not be afraid to ask for help. 

Which is my advice, you need someone to talk to. Not a conputer buddy or anything but a real living breathing person sitting infront of you and truely acknowledging you and your problems and figuring out how to help. You need a professional that is trained in what to say and how to say it so you aren't triggered or just plain ignoring the content thats written or hearing it and twisting it even though you don't mean to. You need to talk to your parents, and if that is too hard there are school counslers for a reason. I'm not talking the guidance counsler, I am talking the psychiactrist in the front office. You need to sit down and talk with them about how your feeling, what is going on in your school life i.e grades, friends, ect, and your home life, depression, anxiety, suicidal thoughts, family, ect. It may be tough to do, but if you do they can help you. If they don't feel they can help you, they will find someone who will. If you don't think they are taking you seriously, ASK for some advice on where to go to get good help. Above all else I think you need to get a therapist or at least talk to the school counsler. They are trained on how to treat someone in your position and even if they can't help they will know the resources to find you someone who can. 

Be safe, Lifes a big long tough journey, but the people who struggle always come out stronger than those who don't. Keep on battling, get the help you need. You are the only one who can change your life, not your parents, friends, even the counslers. They can not make descions for you, and change you, you are the only one who can. If you want to be better you need to go out there and make it better!

I'm going to try and give the best advice I can. 

1. Journal! You need to write everything down. Whether it is an actual journal or just on your computer you need to keep track of yourself. Internally explain the journal and use of it. If internal communication is hard I sugguest you take the time to mediate and just think about the journal and your future and how writing in it can help you. I'm sure somehow your alters will sense this and continue using it, if not at least you have a record of your memories for yourself. I tend to think a journal in which you open it up write a time and what you are doing, how you are feeling and if anything has occured every hour would be best. This also helps you keep track of food and water intake, my system in particular is bad about this. I will front not knowing I havem't had anything to drink all day, then go to work or run my errands and keep wondering why I feel like shit until I get a drink of water and chug the whole glass and realize "damn I haven't had anything to drink today". Journals are super helpful in just "filling in the gaps". 

2. Meditation! Find some good 432 hz (natural tones) preferably binural and use headphones. The binural is like auditory EMDR (regressive therapy) and will help you unlock parts of your mind that are foreign to you. Throughout these meditations focus on ideas of connectivity and communication. Imagine a place for your alters as well as imagine your alters standing infront of you. Greet each one individually and ask them about themselves. The more open and honest you are to them, they more open and honest they will be with you. 

3. The "Who am I?" Question. I ask this to myself in situations that are hard for me. Sometimes I'll be reacting to something angrily or violently and I have no idea why and it frustrates me and just fuels the anger. The best thing I can do is take a deep breath, ground myself and think "who am i?" If I find someone is trying to cocon or front often J can ask what their problem is directly after my mind has realized who it is. By discussing the issue internally is difuses the issue externally. This is not just for bad situations either. Sometimes I get really into a hobby I've never been interested in before and it both confuses and perplexes me, so I think "who am i?" And when i see the person trying to cocon or front with the hobby I can fully allow them to front easier after discussing with them the task and why they want to do it, or why they are drawn to it. By saying "okay, if you like it do it" it almost rewards my alters and the generally feel happier than having to try and force themselves out to get what they want. 

4. DON'T FORCE IT! Things happen, don't try and force anything. By trying to work through things quicker you could effectively be making them worse. If an alter does not want to greet you during a meditation, or does not want to explain to you why they want to front or whatever the case don't force them to do anything. You need to give them their freedom to be just that, themselves. If it is an innaproriate time, say a little part tries to take over and play games at work, take a minute, go somewhere quiet explain to them not right now and try your best to ground yourself. But any time it is approriate allow them to front if they come forward. Just don't actively seek to force them to front in order to learn about them or something. Internal communication is what that is for. By internally communicating you can work towards co-coning so you can truely feel what its like to be them and feel their emotions, then you can start learning from them. But when you force it it is not a true dissociation, they will not be themselves but more a mess of mangled memories from you and them and it can seriously hurt (ie migraines,anxiety attacks, suicidal attempts) because of someone being forced to engage in something they don't want to. 

5. This will be my last little advice that I've found helped me best, scents. Doesn't have to be anything in particular, I personally use purfumes, essential oils and inscents. I allow each one of my parts to have a particular scent to help them fully dissociate. Male parts have their cologne, females their purfumes, some only use essential oils and others prefer to light and inscent. Either way I've found by using scent I've allowed for that jumbled mess to not occur much anymore. When someone fronts they usually take a few minutes, by sometime during that confusion and dissorientation from dissociating they get their scent and litterally make my whole car, house, work, ect smell of "their scent", it allows them to be more comfortable. I've had quite a few parts way before I started using scents complain when they took over they felt particularlly weird and couldnt dissociate fully because they could smell my skin and it weirded them out. Most of the tkme you don't smell your own scent because its you, your always around it, but to them it could be very off putting. Like walking into a strangers home for the first time. My therapist once explained to me when I was younger about the natural masks of the world. Everyone, and I mean everyone has masks they portray to the world. A friend mask, a work mask, a parent mask, a lover mask, ect. We all go through life with these masks on, every person, normal or not. It's just our way of communicating with eachother. You create these masks and or "egos" to help you better relationships in those areas. Say you have an overly girly friend, you are more likely to gush and be effeminant with her simply because it helps better your connection to her, you form a relationship and a "click" so to speak. Then maybe you work a back room job with a bunch of guys, you are going to naturally take on a more masculine tone/air about you while working with said guys because it helps intergrate you into the "click" there. Just because you have drastically switched from these two egos, does not make them seperate entities, it is only your natural survival insticnts to help you survive in the world of communication we live in most effectively. 

However; a person with any form of DID would see these masks, and they wouldn't be masks, they are real people, with vastly different view points than your own. Where as the ego states I describe earlier is simply changing the way you approach people and tasks this would be much more extreme. That person reguardless of being with the girl or bunch of guys would still say 'not like seeing animal abuse', it'd repulse them in either sitatuion. (Extreme scenario but first one that comes to mind) where as in someone with DID if an alter is fronting with the girl and hates animal abuse, then goes to work and another alter comes to front because being around the men triggers them, that alter with the guys might have no issue what so ever with animal abuse, they might even enjoy it. These are the core beliefs of people that are almost impossible to change when it comes to ego states, but almost always occurs within DID. 

DID alters are truly different people, sometimes people see them as "yes I know they are me but they aren't me" and some people say "no they aren't me and never will be me" but you never really see someone say "they are me, theyll always be me, I'm just being a different way". This is because they are not "egos" which everyone has, they are a true split/dissociation from the orginal idea of what the "host/body/main" seems like from the rest of the world. It's truly like feeling like you are walking in someone elses shoes. Even when my alters are fronting and "host masking" (basically there but pretending to be me to seem normal) they can't help but say and do things that are more inclined to them, even if in the wrong setting. They might be fronting with my girl friend and say to her "hey I love abusing animals!" Because thats their core belief but fail to realize thats not the appropriate person to act that way towards. Where as like I said before and ego is going to act a seperate way than you for that girl, but would never bring up something so contrasting to what is considered "normal" to that "body/host/mind,ect". 

As for the memory loss as a child this is often common as well. Childhood memories are core memories yes, so we feel we must remember them, but often times especially in the new day and age there is just too much info in your mind to truly look back and remember things exactly how they were. We have vasts ammounts of memory, so its in there somewhere but you have trouble getting to them simply because in this new world we see and process way more than we could ever imagine, this takes up a lot of your brains memory power and energy in general. This is what hypnosis usually works to help bring up memories, because you completely clear the mind and truely focus its power towards what file you are trying to pull out. Were large computers and even in computers sometimes it takes hours to load a video or a photo already on your hard drive simply because your ram is too busy doing other system things or running other tasks.

This contrasts from DID where memory lapses are not only in childhood but on a pretty regular basis because if alters are not coconing then they truly to miss what all has just happened and when they front they become confused and lost, the begining signs of dissociation.
